approach: Checking that a second run of `swerepo init --only github` changes nothing by running it again with `--yes` on a real repository (dogfooding on an established repository, 2026-11-25).
failure_symptom: The person had just declined applying the GitHub settings in the terminal, so the plan still held the `apply` actions; `--yes` answered them, and the `swerepo` ruleset and merge settings were applied to the live repository without the person's consent (then undone by hand: ruleset deleted, merge settings restored, `[github] applied` set back to false). A second-run check must use `--dry-run` (or compare the plan), never `--yes`, on any repository where the github component runs.
